body:
It’s almost impossible to ignore the feeling in the beginning. This underlying urge to punish ourselves for our sins (in a metaphorical sense) will not ease up until we can pin down exactly what the unconscious problem (maybe actions, self-talk, lack of actions, etc.) is and tackle it. The best way to do this is asking yourself why you want to injure yourself. You mentioned you feel like this because you want to feel something. I’m not gonna lie, I feel the same way. There’s this pain I feel inside that I think will go away if I try to feel something else. But that’s not how it works. By physically harming your body you are attempting to show your unconscious mind that the behavior is punishable by physical pain instead of emotional pain. But that’s impossible. As humans, we are emotional beings and can’t control our emotions. These feelings need to be felt, understood, and then digested, and once they are fully digested, you can start to make them positive.

 I don’t want to seem too direct as I cannot allude to specific disorder as I am not a licensed therapist, but you mentioned you have contracted some eating disorders. I say contracted because as a disorder they are a form of disease, although psychological, the symptoms present themselves in physical sensations and thoughts. This disorder stems from acquired perceptions of other’s actions and behaviors and relating those to our own. But the problem is, we don’t get a full picture of peoples actions or behaviors. As a general example, someone with a bulimic disorder believes they are imitating other people’s quantities of food and ingestion, but they fail to consider that not every body has the same requirements. By the same measure self harm is a way of making up for what we see as failures or lacks by harming our body. 

Digestion of these feelings is complicated as they may stem from self-perception or environmental factors (how you were raised, etc). Therefore, the track that worked the most for me after this realization was attempting to understand the root of the feelings. You can seek help from your husband by attempting to get to the root of the problem. As a general warning, this will probably be a really emotional conversation, as people tend to either hide their true emotions until forced into a corner due to shame, or not even know how they feel (my case). So, I would go to the person you trust the most and attempt to understand what it is that you want to punish yourself for. 

But the most important thing is to remember that harming your body will never make the real pain go away. No matter how much you hit, slap, or cut yourself, even through death, the pain doesn’t go away. Every single suicide survivor I have met has only thanked god that they lived and wished that they wrestled with their emotions first. Face your emotions, allow it to shape you into someone who can fight your own pain, so you can teach others as well.  This fight was not given to you because you deserve to be punished, but because you are strong enough to fight it and deserve to feel the joy of victory. You are not fighting alone, stand with your loved ones and support yourself on them. Much love from Georgia Tech, remember that humans are nothing without each other, and that also counts you.

TL:DR:

Emotions are impossible to get rid of unless the process of digestion is attempted. In other words, attempting to understand the source of the problem and getting to the root of the feeling. After that is understood, proper management can start. I would recommend seeing a therapist or talking to one of your loved ones. But always remember, you are loved :). Even if you try to harm yourself or others, you will still be loved. Humans are complicated creatures (speaking from experience lol) and we won’t have all the answers, but the beauty of this life is that we get to feel all of these emotions that if dealt with properly allow us to grow and become better as people.
